checked.claim: The Cleaning Tool hint and the player handbook promise its tier off a Misleading Trail's 15; the GM scores the trail at 15 whatever the tool.
checked.why: resolveStageSix scores both Stage 6 actions; its relief reads only the row's own toolBonusPerTier, which moveBody alone carries (grep of scripts/ outside the tests: config.mjs:4800 is the field's one definition, cleanup.mjs:1791 its one reader). The tool's tier off a number on any other road is cleanupDc (cleanup.mjs:376), read by the erase and reshape ladder only. The client side arms advantage for every key but moveBody (cleanup.mjs:1671) and sends the roll with dc: def.threshold, 15; the briefing prints CLEANUP.actions.misleadingTrail.threshold plain (action-briefing.mjs:350) and pins it so (tests-tier0.mjs:4904). The player handbook's clean-up section counts the trail as a clean-up (player-handbook.en.md:804) and points to Holding ready for the tool (815), whose line gives the tier off for every clean-up but Move the Body (623); the item hint says the same (config.mjs:691). The GM handbook (1222) names the tier for Move the Body only, agreeing with the code. No test found that scores a trail with a tool in hand. The severity holds: a player's arithmetic is wrong in a particular situation, the GM's card is right.
